360	Rabbi Shlomo asks us: how do I already continue now with the raf"achim, achor
361	and panim, when I haven't yet drawn the mochin to the achor, we haven't yet done the gadlut of the partzufim
362	in the achor, in the achor, that is what I am adding now on your behalf.
363	We haven't yet done the withdrawal, that is, of the nesirah, that
364	is, how do I actually skip over all these stages?
365	So it's true, first of all this proves what we said, that here one kavanes in a more general way.
366	That is, even all the details of Maran the Rashash in the Seder Pidyon Nefesh, for no one in the world has done it
367	like the Rashash, so if I evaluate the Rashash's Seder Pidyon Nefesh in relation
368	to the pidyon nefesh texts written in other books, it's another world, it's far more detailed
369	than anywhere else.
370	And nevertheless, relative to the Rashash himself, Rashash against Rashash, this is considered more general.
371	Now, there are kavanot here that we will kavane as instruction.
372	That is in the instruction, yes?
373	Like for example what he writes later: and to bring them in first into the Nukva and to remove them
374	afterwards, and to bring them in this one, and afterwards... to the Nukva.
375	He writes this here further on.
376	He says it explicitly, but you will kavane it with knowledge.
377	And there are kavanot that are not written here for knowledge, nor as instruction.
378	And the kavanah is that surely this is done according to the order of the levels, as
379	we are accustomed to detail in the Shema and in the Amidah, but
380	here we will kavane it with a general knowledge, what is called "like Rabenu Asher,"
381	okay?
382	Your honor knows the concept "like Rabenu Asher," right?
383	"Like Rabenu Asher" means there is the siddur of Rabenu Asher, which is a siddur
384	called the Siddur HaAri, yes, the regular one,
385	the general one, here I have it right here,
386	this is the Siddur HaAri, yes, of Rabenu Asher, who was one of the sages of Ashkenaz,
387	and the kavanot here are very general,
388	very general, Rabbi Asher Margaliot.
389	And therefore, every place where I don't spell out the details for real, I say: you
390	will kavane this like Rabenu Asher.
391	As if you are praying from the siddur of Rabenu Asher.
392	Very good.
393	So that is regarding this matter.
394	And now, pay close attention.
395	The Rabbi says here: he should kavane that this person,
396	in this world, and like the image of ZoN, ...
397	the person in this world.
398	"You are children to HaShem your Elokeinu."
399	"You are children to HaShem your Elokeinu."
400	The precise wording is: why is it said "You are children to HaShem your Elokeinu"?
401	What, isn't it enough to say "You are children to HaShem"?
402	Rather, everything we say about the Creator, blessed be He, we say from the side of His
403	conducts.
404	In His Essence, blessed be He, there is no grasp of thought at all.
405	Whoever thinks he can speak about His Essence, blessed be He, and define Him with some name or epithet and the like,
406	is making a very serious mistake.
407	He is the one who gives definition and limit to the One without limit.
408	And therefore it is a flaw.
409	Rather, what we define, Kel Rachum VeChanun, Erech Apayim, HaShem, Elokeichem,
410	Shakai, Kel, Tzevakot, Ehyeh and the like, everything we speak of is only in the conducts that emanate from Him,
411	blessed be He.
412	And this is what the Holy One, blessed be He, says to Moshe Rabenu: "You seek to know My name; by the name of
413	My deeds I am called."
414	By the name of My deeds I am called, that is, all the names you know are the names of my deeds.
415	It is not His Essence, blessed be He, it is not My name, I have no name.
416	These are the names of my actions, of my deeds, toward you.
417	For my actions, my deeds, in fact come according to the limit of
418	the created beings.
419	Yes?
420	Each and every thing.
421	So when it is written "your Elokeichem," these are conducts.
422	There is the conduct of Havayah, there is the conduct of Elokim.
423	In the sefirot it is called Tiferet and Malchut, in the partzufim it is called ZA and Nukva, and these are the conducts
424	that are toward the lower human beings, us, and therefore it is written "You are children
425	to HaShem your Elokeichem," these are those conducts, which are called ZoN.
426	And the Rabbi says here: "You are children to HaShem your Elokeichem," and he should kavane to purify
427	from the sick person the beirurim of achor and panim, pay attention, he should kavane
428	to purify from the sick person the beirurim of achor and panim,
429	from the Heichal of Ahavah-Chesed, and from the Heichal of Kodesh Kodashim,
430	of ZoN of Beriah, of Abba, of Abba, the kavanah of inner
431	and outer aspects, and to give himself over for the sanctification of the Name,
432	and to accept upon himself the four deaths of Beit Din, and to raise them
433	for the sake of... until here.
434	So what do we have here?
435	Pay close attention.
436	To purify beirurim, soon we will stop here on a few precisions, yes?
437	To purify beirurim from the sick person.
438	Why?
439	Because the mochin of gadlut have withdrawn from this sick person.
440	They want to draw the mochin of gadlut.
441	So to kavane to purify beirurim, meaning those that belong to the sick person.
442	Since one must kavane to purify beirurim that belong to the sick person, therefore surely there is great significance
443	in the pidyon money coming out of the sick person's pocket.
444	Because by the sick person giving the money, he is in fact
445	giving tzedakah.
446	This is in fact the giving of tzedakah that he gives.
447	Giving tzedakah, gentlemen, yes?
448	It is a general act, only truly...
449	Air, do you want the air conditioner or the window?
450	Yes, the Rabbi is standing there, let us have a bit, let there be a bit of air, I
451	say.
452	Huh?
453	Yes, yes, with HaShem's help.
454	Everything, let there be a strong wind.
455	Perfectly fine.
456	And if it will harm the sick person?
457	Wait, one second, gentlemen.
458	Therefore there is significance in this truly coming from the sick person himself, so that it will in fact be
459	the tzedakah.
460	Tzedakah, there is a lot about this in the Torah of the Baal HaTanya, and also in many other books
461	of tzaddikim, which explain that giving tzedakah is a general mitzvah, which has
462	the power to purify the beirurim, no matter with what
463	sin the sick person caused damage.
464	For what is the matter?
465	The matter is...
466	That now, for example, the sick person sinned in a certain transgression, right?
467	Now, what must he do?
468	He must do teshuvah for that transgression in which he sinned.
469	That is certain.
470	But if he doesn't know what he sinned in, how can he do some thing that he knows that...
471	How do you say?
472	Whatever it may be, grasp.
473	I can that it will help.
474	One of these mitzvot, he can do teshuvah in a general way.
475	I return in teshuvah, Master of the World, for everything I sinned, whether what I know or what I don't know.
476	That is excellent.
477	And truly the sick person must do this.
478	If he gives tzedakah without teshuvah, without even at least stirring himself to teshuvah, then this
479	is a problem.
